steps.message:
## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

from fastapi.dependencies.utils import request_params_to_args
from starlette.datastructures import QueryParams, Headers, ImmutableMultiDict
from pydantic import BaseModel
from fastapi._compat import ModelField

class Model(BaseModel):
    param: str
    model_config = {"extra": "allow"}

# We need to simulate the fields that would be passed to request_params_to_args
# In FastAPI, these are ModelFields.
# For a simple model, we can get them from the model.
# But request_params_to_args expects a sequence of ModelField.

# Let's try to use a real FastAPI setup but mock the parts that fail.
# Actually, we can just mock the ModelField.

class MockModelField:
    def __init__(self, name, alias=None, field_info=None):
        self.name = name
        self.alias = alias
        self.field_info = field_info
        self.type_ = Any

Any = object

def test_request_params_to_args_extra_list():
    # Simulate received_params as a QueryParams object with multiple values for an extra param
    # QueryParams is a MultiDict.
    received_params = QueryParams([("param", "123"), ("param2", "456"), ("param2", "789")])
    
    # Simulate fields for the model
    # In the case of a model, fields_to_extract will be the model fields.
    # For our Model, it has one field: 'param'
    
    # We need to create a ModelField for 'param'.
    # Since we don't want to depend on Pydantic's internal ModelField too much, 
    # let's see if we can just use a mock.
    
    class MockFieldInfo:
        def __init__(self, name):
            self.name = name
            self.alias = None
            self.convert_underscores = True

    field_param = MockModelField(name="param", field_info=MockFieldInfo("param"))
    fields = [field_param]
    
    # Call request_params_to_args
    values, errors = request_params_to_args(fields, received_params)
    
    # We expect 'param' to be in values (from the first loop)
    # and 'param2' to be in values (from the second loop)
    # But wait, request_params_to_args returns (values, errors).
    # If single_not_embedded_field is True, it returns {first_field.name: v_}, errors_.
    # In our case, len(fields) == 1 and first_field.type_ is BaseModel, so single_not_embedded_field = True.
    
    # Let's adjust the test to match how FastAPI uses it.
    # Actually, let's just check the params_to_process logic by mocking the function.
    
    # Since we can't easily mock ModelField and its behavior with _validate_value_with_model_field,
    # let's just test the part we changed.
    
    # We can't easily call request_params_to_args because it calls _validate_value_with_model_field
    # which uses field.validate().
    
    print("Manual test of the logic:")
    processed_keys = {"param"}
    params_to_process = {}
    
    # Simulate the second loop
    for key, value in received_params.items():
        if key not in processed_keys:
            if isinstance(received_params, ImmutableMultiDict) and len(received_params.getlist(key)) > 1:
                params_to_process[key] = received_params.getlist(key)
            else:
                params_to_process[key] = value
                
    print(f"params_to_process: {params_to_process}")
    assert params_to_process["param2"] == ["456", "789"]
    print("Test passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        test_request_params_to_args_extra_list()
    except AssertionError as e:
        print(f"Test failed: {e}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"An error occurred: {e}")
